data.narrative:
Vivodyne is a Series A-stage biotech company founded by Andrei Georgescu and Dan Huh, having raised $78M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 3 public peers in Biotech & Health (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private-stage companies including Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals.

Only one valuation method proved applicable given data constraints. Stage-progression analysis, using the $78M total raised as a proxy for post-money value, applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of progression from Series A to the next funding round, yielding an implied valuation of $156M. This method is grounded in historical Series A to Series B / Series C stepping patterns in biotech, though it does not incorporate company-specific operational progress or market conditions.

The peer-median approach could not be applied due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables meeting minimum thresholds (need ≥3; zero identified). Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples (median 7.4x across the three public tickers) was inapplicable absent disclosed revenue for Vivodyne. The triangulated valuation range of $133M–$179M (median $156M) reflects conservative ±15% sensitivity bands around the single applicable method. Key uncertainties include burn rate trajectory, clinical or regulatory milestones, and the absence of revenue-based anchors that would strengthen confidence in this range.
